results.description: Description of an access method (i.e. communication protocol) that can be used to fetch a File object (orig: DrsObject). Exact copy of the AccessMethod object of the GA4GH DRS data model.

Access protocols (i.e. communication protocols) for fetching a data file, following the vocabulary defined in the GA4GH DRS specification (renamed from the FGA-WG enum AccessMethods to avoid the near-clash with the AccessMethod class).
The URL and associated HTTP headers to access the File object (orig: DrsObject). Exact copy of AccessURL object of the GA4GH DRS data model.

Represents the computational processing applied to data from a sequencing experiment, or from another analysis. This can be described at the level of individual analysis steps in a workflow/pipeline, or more generally for the workflow/pipeline as a whole. Boundary with TrackProvenance: TrackProvenance (Layer 2) carries faceted, closed-vocabulary descriptors of what was done to the CONTENT (read selection, filtering, normalization, ...); Analysis is the record of the ACTIVITY itself (workflow, tool, version, inputs). Complementary, not competing.
The linkml:Any allows the range of a slot to be any object (see https://linkml.io/linkml/schemas/advanced.html#linkml-any-type).
Key-value pair representing a specific value produced by a quality assessment.
Vocabulary from the ENCODE model describing the general category of biospecimen (see "Properties->classification" in https://www.encodeproject.org/profiles/biosample_type).
A checksum of a File object (orig: DrsObject). Exact copy of the Checksum object of the GA4GH DRS data model.
Contact information for a person or an organisation.

Computational output types - the data structure or processing result 
a file contains. Describes HOW data was produced or represented.
Examples: peaks (output of peak caller), signal track, alignments, count matrix.
Information about a public deposit of a document containing metadata about a set of genome annotation files.

The epistemic origin of a file's values — empirically observed (measured from experimental data) vs. computationally predicted (generated by a model) — factored out of the compound ENCODE output_type / DataType / FeatureType terms. A provenance facet recording how the values were obtained, not what they mean. Absent means unspecified (not a default of observed). `control` is deliberately excluded: it denotes an experimental role or normalization reference, not the measured-vs-model axis.

Information about a document containing metadata about a set of genome annotation files, harmonised according to this schema. This includes self-referential identifiers and versioning of public deposits of the document.
Information about the donor or complete organism from which the sample was taken.

Represents a sequencing experiment that has been carried out within a study, based on biological samples, and providing data files as output. Subsequent analysis of output data is described by the Analysis entity. Assay properties (assay_type, antibody_target, instrument, ...) live HERE, on the investigation-layer Experiment record — not in the ONGA content vocabularies, consistent with ONGA design principle #5 (sample and assay properties are out of scope for the content vocabularies).

Biological feature types - the biological entity or concept the data 
represents. Describes WHAT biological phenomenon the features capture.
Examples: enhancers, TF binding sites, methylation states, chromatin loops.

General information about a particular data file. Most fields (marked with an asterix*) are copied from the GA4GH DRS DrsObject model, which is the top-level object returned from a DRS server in response to a successful lookup call (i.e. https://ga4gh.github.io/data-repository-service-schemas/preview/release/drs-1.4.0/docs/#tag/Objects).

A collection of files, according to some selection criteria. Mainly intended for GenomicAnnotationFile entities, but other types of files can also be contained in a collection, e.g. raw data files such as FASTQ files. This is the natural future home for the BEDset concept (a curated collection of BED files).

The quality-control filtering status of the data a file represents, factored out of the compound ENCODE output_type / DataType terms. Applies across output types (reads, alignments, peaks, variants, quantifications, count matrices).
Common file formats for genomic annotation tracks. Where an EDAM term exists for the format, it is referenced via `meaning`.

Information about a genomic annotation / track file. GenomicAnnotationFile is a specification of the File entity and inherits all the fields defined in File, in addition to the fields that are specific to GenomicAnnotationFile, as detailed here. This is the class that composes the five ONGA descriptor schemas: the required reference_genome (the coordinate system) plus the recommended track_format, track_interpretation, track_provenance, and track_geometry descriptors.
Haplotype resolution of a genomic annotation track, factored out of the compound ENCODE / DataType / FeatureType terms. Absent means haplotype-collapsed / not phase-resolved.

General object representing the source of data files, samples, or other entities used as input to a process or a result. An input source refering to a single file or sample object will represent that item only, while an input source referring to a container or process may represent a number of disctinct input items. InputSource also contains information about the type of relationship, replication labelling, versioning and retrieval date. The qualified_relation values are typically PROV CURIEs (prov:wasDerivedFrom, prov:used, prov:wasGeneratedBy, ...) carried as data-level cross-references.

The scaling normalization applied to a signal, factored out of the compound ENCODE output_type / DataType terms. A provenance facet recording the scaling operation applied to produce the values. Absent means unspecified (not raw). Does not cover statistic transforms (p-value, fold-change, z-score, enrichment) or smoothing, which are distinct output_types.

Information about an ontology used in the metadata: a map from the version-agnostic URL to a versioned URL. Version pinning is real work for deposit documents — the OWL versionIRI mechanism serves the same purpose at the ontology level.

Represents the results of a quality assessment that has been carried out on a data file resulting from an experiment or analysis. This is the natural home for repository QC metrics (e.g. BEDbase BedStats numbers). A typed QC vocabulary may later tighten assessment_method; for now it accepts a free string or a Term.
The read mapping-multiplicity subset used to compute a signal or count track (all mapped reads vs uniquely-mapping reads only), factored out of the compound ENCODE output_type / DataType terms.

The sex of the reference genome build used (which sex chromosomes the assembly contains), factored out of compound ENCODE output_type / DataType terms. A property of the reference assembly, NOT of the biological sample. Absent means unspecified / sex-neutral combined assembly.

ONGA descriptor schema for the reference genome a track is defined against (FGA-issue-adjacent: every genomic annotation is relative to a reference assembly). Carries content-derived seqcol digests and human-readable identifiers for the exact assembly, plus the sex of the reference build (factored out of compound terms like "male genome reference"). The build sex is a property of the reference assembly, NOT of the biological sample (that is Donor.donor_sex). Absorbs the FGA-WG GenomeAssembly class.

Information about a biospecimen/sample used as raw material for lab experiments. Sample properties are ontology-delegated via Term-valued slots (UBERON for tissue, CL for cell type, CLO for cell line, PATO for phenotype), per ONGA design principle #5.
Strand orientation of a genomic annotation track, factored out of the compound ENCODE output_type / DataType terms.
A scientific study, i.e. a unit of research, within which experiments and/or analyses have been carried out.

Helper entity to represent an ontology term as a data value. Term instances are DATA-LEVEL cross-references: a CURIE carried inside a record, never a schema-level IRI. Schema-level cross-references use mapping slots (exact_mappings/close_mappings/broad_mappings) per ONGA design principle #7, never `meaning:`.

The retention cut applied to produce a file and the basis of that cut, factored out of the compound ENCODE output_type / DataType terms. A provenance facet recording that a threshold was applied. Absent means no threshold / unspecified. Cross-cuts peaks, contact matrices, and regulatory links.
A document of harmonised metadata for a set of genome annotation files. This is the top-level class to be used as root for a metadata deposit document.
How a genomic annotation file is encoded: its primary file format and, for BED-family formats, the number of standard (core) and extra (custom) columns. Corresponds to FGA-WG issue #1.

Overall geometric properties of the sequence features in the genomic annotation file if considered as an one-dimensional genome browser track, in line with the track type delineations from Gundersen et. al, 2011. While conceptually based on visual characteristics, these properties are also useful to e.g. select relevant annotation files for non-visual analyses.

What the data in a genomic annotation file represents, split into an algorithmic interpretation (output_type, drawing on the DataType vocabulary) and a biological interpretation (feature_type, drawing on the FeatureType vocabulary). Corresponds to FGA-WG issue #2.

The processing/derivation operations applied to the data to produce the file: which read subset it was computed from (read_multiplicity), what QC filtering operation was applied (filter_status), and what scaling normalization was applied (normalization), what retention cut / thresholding was applied (thresholding), and the epistemic origin of the values (derivation: observed vs. predicted). This schema is the planned home for further processing facets as they are decided. Boundary with the Analysis record class (Layer 4): TrackProvenance carries faceted, closed-vocabulary descriptors of what was done to the CONTENT; Analysis is the record of the ACTIVITY itself (workflow, tool, version, inputs). Complementary, not competing.
Types of data values associated with sequence features or edges. (Renamed from the FGA-WG enum DataTypes to avoid the near-clash with the ONGA DataType content vocabulary.)
